questions.question: Define the rate of flow of heat. Write its formula and SI unit.
questions.solution:
**Definition:** The rate of flow of heat (heat current) is defined as the amount of heat flowing through a cross-section per unit time.
$$\boxed{\text{Rate of heat flow} = \frac{Q}{t} = \frac{mc\Delta\theta}{t}}$$

**SI unit:** $\text{J s}^{-1} = $ watt (W). The cgs unit is **calorie per second (cal/s)**.

**Note:** The rate at which heat flows is directly proportional to the temperature difference. If $Q$ is in joules and $t$ in seconds, $H = Q/t$ in watts; the rate per unit area is the **heat current density** in $\text{W m}^{-2}$.
questions.knowledgeNote: Rate of heat flow is heat divided by time, measured in watts (joules per second).
